chunks: They will be the unbelievers, transgressors.

key_terms.أُولَٰئِكَ: Those (demonstrative pronoun pointing to a specific group)
key_terms.الْفَجَرَةُ: The transgressors/wicked (plural of fajir, those who exceed bounds in sin)
key_terms.الْكَفَرَةُ: The disbelievers (plural of kafir, those who cover/deny the truth)

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'kafarah' and 'fajarah' mentioned in Surah Abasa?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the incident of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ frowning at Ibn Umm Maktum, highlighting how the elite's neglect of the humble reflects spiritual arrogance. The terms 'al-kafarah' and 'al-fajarah' denote not just disbelief but active moral transgression, serving as a critique of social hierarchy that ignores sincere devotion.
